# Differential corpus for the CFITSIO expression parser.
#
# One expression per line. Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored;
# there is no way to write a comment on the same line as an expression, and no
# expression may contain a leading '#' (use the constant forms below, which are
# listed with a leading space-free '#' only inside a larger expression).
#
# Table schema (see tests/test_eval_corpus.rs), 3 rows:
#   INTCOL   1J    7, -3, 10
#   FLOATCOL 1E    2.5, 4.0, 0.5
#   STRCOL   10A   "abc", "de", "fghij"
#   BOOLCOL  1L    T, F, T
#   DBLCOL   1D    1.25, -2.5, 8.0
#   VECCOL   3E    {1,2,3} {4,5,6} {7,8,9}
#   BITS     8X    0xF0, 0x0F, 0xAA
#   MATRIX   6E    2x3, 1..6 / 11..16 / 21..26
# keywords: INTKEY=42, DBLKEY=2.5, LOGKEY=T, STRKEY='hello'

ACCUM(INTCOL)
ACCUM(FLOATCOL)
# ACCUM(BOOLCOL) and ACCUM(BITS) are omitted: the grammar lowers them to a
# LONG binop over a char-valued operand, so Do_BinOp_lng reads a char buffer
# through a *long pointer.  CFITSIO returns garbage (ACCUM(bool) -> 65537) and
# the Rust debug build traps on the misaligned read.  Pre-existing defect in
# the evaluation engine, unrelated to the parser -- see the migration notes.
SEQDIFF(INTCOL)
SEQDIFF(FLOATCOL)

# ===================================================================
# 8. Binary operator x operand-sort matrix
# Every operator against every pair of sorts.  eval.y accepts a different
# subset for each: '+' has three productions (expr, sexpr, bits), '*' also
# takes expr*bexpr, '&&' only bexpr, and comparisons differ between the
# ordering and equality groups.  This is the grid that catches a sort
# predicate being wrong in one operator but right in its neighbour.
# ===================================================================
